quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Nitin Agrawal): revenue was $1.6 billion, up 110% year-over-year; full-year 2025 revenue was approximately $5.1 billion, up 168%. Adjusted EBITDA was $898 million (57% margin); adjusted operating income was $88 million (6% margin), lower than expected 'as a result of deploying infrastructure ahead of our expectations'. Net loss was $452 million. CEO says CoreWeave is 'the fastest cloud in history to reach $5 billion in annual revenue'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $1.6 billion (+110%); FY2025 revenue approximately $5.1 billion (+168%); adjusted EBITDA $898 million (57%); adjusted operating income $88 million (6%); net loss $452 million

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted revenue backlog grew to $66.8 billion, up $11.2 billion sequentially and more than $50 billion year-over-year ('up more than 4x this year alone'). Every contract for new capacity is expected to begin generating revenue by year-end 2026. Weighted average contract length rose 'from roughly 4 years to roughly 5 years'. Customers committed to spending at least $1 million grew by nearly 150% in 2025, and Q4 added approximately twice as many new reserved instance customers as any prior quarter (AI native and enterprise names cited include Cognition, Cursor, Mercado Libre, Midjourney and Runway); both existing hyperscale cloud customers (not named) expanded.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $66.8 billion (+$11.2 billion QoQ, more than $50 billion YoY); contract length roughly 4 years to roughly 5 years; customers committed to at least $1 million up nearly 150%

quarterly_data.signal: Capex in Q4 totaled $8.2 billion and $14.9 billion for the full year, above guidance because infrastructure was put in service ahead of expectations. Construction in progress grew to $9.4 billion, up $2.5 billion quarter-over-quarter. The large majority of term debt is structured as delayed draw facilities drawn only as data centers are operationalized.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 capex $8.2 billion; FY2025 capex $14.9 billion; construction in progress $9.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance: CapEx of $30 billion to $35 billion ('more than double our 2025 investment'), substantially all tied to already signed customer contracts; active power expected to double to more than 1.7 gigawatts by year-end. FY2026 revenue $12 billion to $13 billion (approximately 140% growth at the midpoint); adjusted operating income $900 million to $1.1 billion, with margins at a Q1 trough in the low single digits and returning to low double digits by Q4. Q1 2026: revenue $1.9 billion to $2 billion, adjusted operating income between $0 and $40 million, capex $6 billion to $7 billion, interest expense $510 million to $590 million. Exit-2026 annualized run rate revenue of $17 billion to $19 billion, growing to more than $30 billion exiting 2027. Guidance excludes licensing of the proprietary cloud stack.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx $30 billion to $35 billion; 2026 revenue $12 billion to $13 billion; adj. operating income $900 million to $1.1 billion; Q1 revenue $1.9 billion to $2 billion; exit-2026 run rate $17 billion to $19 billion; more than $30 billion exiting 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Power footprint: more than 850 megawatts of active power at December 31, adding approximately 260 megawatts in Q4 across 43 active data centers (up from 32 at the start of the year). Contracted close to 2 gigawatts of additional power in 2025, ending with more than 3.1 gigawatts of contracted capacity, virtually all expected online by the end of 2027 (CEO: 1.3 gigawatts in the portfolio at the end of 2024). New objective of adding more than 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity beyond the contracted footprint by 2030. Q4's additions were 'fully 1/3 of our installed capacity'.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 850 megawatts active; approximately 260 megawatts added in Q4; 43 active data centers; more than 3.1 gigawatts contracted; more than 5 gigawatts additional by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Prior-generation GPUs remain supply constrained with rising demand, largely for inference: average H100 pricing in Q4 was within 10% of where it started the year, while average A100 pricing increased in 2025. CFO, referring to the CEO's remarks, said Hoppers are being recontracted 'at about 10% of the original ASPs' (as transcribed; inconsistent with the CEO's prepared statement that average H100 pricing was within 10% of its start-of-year level) while A100 ASPs are increasing on new contracts. CoreWeave is 'virtually sold out in 2026 of all of our capacity' with largely all new 2026 capacity allocated. Pricing remained stable throughout 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: H100 pricing within 10% of start of year; A100 pricing increased in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Margin framework: mature, fully ramped contracts generate contribution margins in the mid-20s and EBITDA margins 'in the 70-percentage zone'; long-term target of 25% to 30% margins as growth normalizes. Weighted average interest rate fell 300 basis points in 2025 (nearly $700 million in annualized interest savings on the Q4 debt balance). Q4 financing: approximately $2.6 billion inaugural convertible notes; revolver expanded to $2.5 billion; more than $18 billion of debt and equity secured in 2025; cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities $4.2 billion; no debt maturities until 2029 other than self-amortizing contract-backed debt and OEM vendor financing.
quarterly_data.figure: contribution margins mid-20s; long-term margins 25% to 30%; 300 basis points rate decline (nearly $700 million savings); more than $18 billion raised in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Platform monetization beyond GPUs: approximately 80% of customers paying at least $1 million per year have adopted one or more storage products (storage revenue eclipsed $100 million in ARR, announced in Q3); Weights & Biases cross-selling added hundreds of millions of CoreWeave Cloud TCV in 2H25. Select customers license SUNK as their default research cluster management platform across multi-cloud footprints; licensing the proprietary cloud stack (SUNK, Mission Control) to other NVIDIA cloud, enterprise and sovereign customers is expected to begin in 2026 and is excluded from guidance. Four strategic acquisitions completed in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 80% storage attach among customers paying at least $1 million per year; storage ARR above $100 million

players.product: GB200 / GB300 / Vera Rubin GPU systems

contracts.signal: CoreWeave CFO: in January CoreWeave announced the expansion of its commercial relationship with NVIDIA, accompanied by a $2 billion investment in CoreWeave. CEO: NVIDIA intends to test and validate CoreWeave's platform, software and reference architectures toward including them in NVIDIA's reference architecture for cloud, enterprise and sovereign customers; CoreWeave will 'selectively leverage our expanded collaboration with NVIDIA' to accelerate its capacity roadmap, and working with an investment-grade counterparty as the offtake lowers data-center costs, and CoreWeave works with NVIDIA on its data center build-out 'selectively, but certainly not exclusively'.

quarterly_data.signal: Blackwell execution: the Q3 data center delays were cleared and CoreWeave has now delivered more than 50,000 Grace Blackwells to the impacted customer (not named), deploying servers within weeks of receiving data center access. In Q4 CoreWeave became the first cloud platform to reach NVIDIA's Exemplar Cloud Status for GB200. Operations span more than 100,000 GPUs. CEO: 'it is early in the deployment of Grace Blackwell' and few clusters exist at the scale CoreWeave has already delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 50,000 Grace Blackwells delivered to one customer; first cloud to Exemplar Cloud Status for GB200

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: CoreWeave expects to be one of the first to bring NVIDIA's new Rubin GPU platform to market in the second half of 2026, while expanding its product portfolio to include NVIDIA's Vera CPU and BlueField storage, to power capabilities including agentic workflows. CFO: commitments span current and past GPU generations 'with active conversations already underway for future SKUs'; Asked about Rubin contracts, the CEO said customers' growing confidence in infrastructure longevity is extending contracts (average four to five years) and that CoreWeave adjusts its pricing as infrastructure prices change to target the margins the CFO described (not a Rubin-specific price).

players.product: specialized GPU cloud for AI labs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: demand is moving from 'just the GPU' out 'into storage, into CPUs' as customers extend into the application layer; AI native and enterprise customers engage 'at significantly higher rates across CPU, storage, software, and development tools'. CoreWeave plans to add NVIDIA's Vera CPU to its product portfolio alongside Rubin in the second half of 2026.
